title: CelluWeave D：低温储存后的可逆性
researchQuestion: Evaluation of the mechanical stability and shape retention of a sodium alginate and cellulose hydrogel after cold storage.
mainFindings: After 7 days of storage at 4°C, the mean compression modulus of the material was 46.0 kPa.
The shape retention rate of the material after 7 days of storage at 4°C was 95%.
The mean compression modulus decreased by 4.0 kPa, representing an 8.0% reduction compared to fresh samples.
The compression modulus mean was 46.0 kPa (SD 2.0 kPa, n=4) after 7 days of storage at 4°C.
Fresh samples had a mean compression modulus of 50.0 kPa (n=4).
methods: Formulation of sodium alginate 2.0% and cellulose 1.2%
Curing with 50 mmol/L calcium chloride for 10 minutes
Mechanical testing in wet state after 24-hour equilibrium at 10% strain
methodsSummary: The study utilized a material composed of 2.0% sodium alginate and 1.2% cellulose, cured with 50 mmol/L calcium chloride for 10 minutes. The material was stored at 4°C for 7 days and then tested for compression modulus and shape retention under 10% strain after 24 hours of wet-state equilibrium.

shortSummary: This study evaluated a sodium alginate and cellulose hydrogel, finding that after 7 days of storage at 4°C, it retained 95% of its shape and experienced only an 8% decrease in compression modulus.
